theme: The Byzantine Empire: Constantinople & Eastern Rome
title: The Byzantine Empire: Constantinople & Eastern Rome
description: A 60-question grand master assessment on Hagia Sophia, Greek Fire, Justinian Code, Empress Theodora, Theodosian Walls, and 1453.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor founded Constantinople in 330 CE as the new capital of the Roman Empire?
questions.explanation: Constantine established Nova Roma on the site of ancient Byzantium, soon renamed Constantinople in his honor.

questions.question: What monumental cathedral with a colossal dome was built in Constantinople under Emperor Justinian I in 537 CE?
questions.explanation: Hagia Sophia (Holy Wisdom) was designed by architects Isidore of Miletus and Anthemius of Tralles and remained the world largest cathedral for nearly a millennium.

questions.question: What deadly incendiary naval weapon, able to burn on water, defended Constantinople from maritime sieges?
questions.explanation: Greek Fire was a secret petroleum-based incendiary formula pressurized through siphons that ignited spontaneously on seawater.

questions.question: Which Byzantine legal masterpiece codified centuries of Roman civil jurisprudence between 529 and 534 CE?
questions.explanation: The Corpus Juris Civilis, compiled under Justinian direction by jurist Tribonian, formed the basis of modern European civil law.

questions.question: Who was the influential Byzantine empress and wife of Justinian I who famously halted the Nika Riots?
questions.explanation: Theodora famously declared that the imperial purple makes a fine burial shroud, convincing Justinian to stand firm during the 532 CE revolt.

questions.question: In what year CE was the grand cathedral of Hagia Sophia officially inaugurated in Constantinople?
questions.explanation: Hagia Sophia was consecrated on December 27, 537 CE after just under six years of intensive construction.

questions.question: What massive triple-layered defensive walls protected Constantinople from landward assaults for over a millennium?
questions.explanation: The Theodosian Walls, built under Emperor Theodosius II in the 5th century, resisted numerous sieges by Avars, Persians, and Arabs.

questions.question: Which Byzantine emperor earned the moniker Bulgar Slayer after his victorious Balkan military campaigns in 1014 CE?
questions.explanation: Basil II reigned during the Byzantine golden age, expanding the empire from southern Italy to the Caucasus and defeating the Bulgarian kingdom.

questions.question: What tragic historic event in 1204 CE saw Western crusaders divert from the Holy Land to sack Constantinople?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Crusade assaulted Christian Constantinople in 1204, establishing the short-lived Latin Empire and fracturing Byzantine power.

questions.question: What was the primary language of administration, literature, and culture in the Byzantine Empire from the 7th century onward?
questions.explanation: Under Emperor Heraclius in the 620s CE, medieval Greek replaced Latin as the official imperial language.

questions.question: Which iconic golden coin served as the reliable international currency of the Mediterranean world for centuries?
questions.explanation: The gold Solidus (or Nomisma) maintained strict purity for over 700 years, nicknamed the dollar of the Middle Ages.

questions.question: In what year CE did Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II conquer Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire?
questions.explanation: Constantinople fell on May 29, 1453, marking the conclusion of over 1,100 years of the Eastern Roman Empire.

questions.question: What chariot racing stadium and civic hub in Constantinople could hold over 60,000 cheering spectators?
questions.explanation: The Hippodrome was the social center of Constantinople where rival political factions known as the Blues and Greens competed.

questions.question: Which Byzantine emperor recovered the True Cross from the Sassanid Persian Empire in 628 CE after a grueling war?
questions.explanation: Heraclius executed daring deep offensive campaigns into Persia, reclaiming Jerusalem and holy relics.

questions.question: What theological dispute over religious imagery divided the Byzantine Empire and church throughout the 8th and 9th centuries?
questions.explanation: Iconoclasm involved state-sponsored destruction of religious icons and paintings initiated by Emperor Leo III in 726 CE.

questions.question: Which Byzantine princess wrote the Alexiad, a detailed 15-volume historical account of her father reign and the First Crusade?
questions.explanation: Anna Komnene is widely celebrated as one of the very first female historians of the Western and medieval world.

questions.question: What famous subterranean water reservoir supported by 336 marble columns was built beneath Constantinople under Justinian?
questions.explanation: The Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarayi) could store over 80,000 cubic meters of fresh water delivered via aqueducts.

questions.question: Approximately how many marble columns support the vaulted ceiling of the Basilica Cistern in Constantinople?
questions.explanation: The Basilica Cistern features 336 carved marble columns arranged in 12 rows of 28 columns each.

questions.question: Which brilliant Byzantine general reconquered North Africa from the Vandals and Italy from the Ostrogoths for Justinian?
questions.explanation: Flavius Belisarius was one of history greatest tactical generals, executing campaigns with minimal troop losses.

questions.question: What massive chain was drawn across the water to protect Constantinople harbor from enemy fleets during sieges?
questions.explanation: A heavy iron chain supported by wooden floats was stretched across the Golden Horn from Constantinople to Galata.

questions.question: What formal religious schism in 1054 CE permanently split the Christian Church into Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox branches?
questions.explanation: Mutual excommunications between Cardinal Humbert and Patriarch Michael Keroularios in 1054 finalized the Great Schism.

questions.question: Which ruling dynasty founded by Michael VIII Palaiologos ruled Byzantium from 1261 until its final fall in 1453?
questions.explanation: The Palaiologan Dynasty was the longest-ruling and final imperial dynasty of the Byzantine Empire.

questions.question: What Byzantine silk industry secret was smuggled from China by Christian monks during Justinian reign?
questions.explanation: Smuggled silkworm eggs hidden in hollow walking canes established a lucrative Byzantine imperial monopoly on silk production.

questions.question: In what year CE did the Great Schism formally separate Eastern Orthodox Christianity from the Roman Catholic Church?
questions.explanation: The Great East-West Schism occurred in July 1054 CE at Hagia Sophia in Constantinople.

questions.question: What famous purple stone quarried in Egypt was reserved exclusively for imperial Byzantine births and tombs?
questions.explanation: Children born to reigning emperors in the purple porphyry-lined chamber were called Porphyrogennetos (Born in the Purple).

questions.question: Which Byzantine emperor appealed to Pope Urban II in 1095 for Western military assistance against Seljuk Turks, sparking the First Crusade?
questions.explanation: Emperor Alexios I Komnenos sent envoys to the Council of Piacenza, leading to the mobilization of the First Crusade.

questions.question: What administrative and military system divided the Byzantine Empire into regional military districts commanded by generals?
questions.explanation: The Theme system granted hereditary plots of farmland to citizen-soldiers in exchange for regional military defense.

questions.question: Which last reigning Byzantine emperor died heroically in battle during the final Ottoman assault on the walls of Constantinople?
questions.explanation: Constantine XI tore off his imperial insignia and led a final charge into the breaches near the Gate of Saint Romanus.

questions.question: What natural body of water separates the European side of Constantinople from the Asian coastline of Anatolia?
questions.explanation: The Bosphorus Strait connects the Black Sea to the Sea of Marmara, providing Constantinople with unmatched maritime control.

questions.question: How many total days did the historic final Ottoman siege of Constantinople last in the spring of 1453?
questions.explanation: The Ottoman siege began on April 6, 1453, and concluded with the breach of the city on May 29, lasting 53 days.

questions.question: Which Byzantine missionary brothers invented the Glagolitic script and translated scripture for Slavic peoples in the 9th century?
questions.explanation: Saints Cyril and Methodius created the writing system that evolved into the modern Cyrillic alphabet used across Eastern Europe.

questions.question: What grand palace complex served as the primary residence of Byzantine emperors from Constantine until the 11th century?
questions.explanation: The Great Palace of Constantinople was a sprawling complex of reception halls, gardens, and churches adjacent to the Hippodrome.

questions.question: What famous artistic medium featuring colored glass and gold leaf tesserae adorned Byzantine church walls and apses?
questions.explanation: Byzantine masters angled glittering gold glass tesserae to capture flickering candlelight, creating breathtaking divine atmospheres.

questions.question: Which medieval Italian maritime republic dominated Byzantine commercial trade concessions after receiving the Golden Bull in 1082?
questions.explanation: Venetian merchants gained duty-free trading rights across Byzantine ports in exchange for naval defense against Norman invaders.

questions.question: What ancient city fortified on the Peloponnese peninsula served as the final cultural capital of the Byzantine Despotate of the Morea?
questions.explanation: Mistras was a vibrant center of late Byzantine art and Neo-Platonic philosophy under scholars like Gemistos Plethon.

questions.question: In what year CE did the Fourth Crusade violently conquer and plunder the city of Constantinople?
questions.explanation: Crusaders breached Constantinople seaward walls on April 12, 1204, carrying off irreplaceable classical and Christian relics.

questions.question: What defensive military horn trumpet signal was used by Byzantine infantry to coordinate disciplined phalanx maneuvers?
questions.explanation: The Strategikon of Maurice detailed Byzantine tactical doctrines, battlefield signals, and combined-arms military manuals.

questions.question: Which Byzantine emperor composed the De Administrando Imperio, a confidential geopolitical manual for his son?
questions.explanation: Constantine VII compiled state secrets and diplomatic strategies for dealing with Pechenegs, Magyars, Rus, and Arabs.

questions.question: What great military manual written around 600 CE is attributed to Emperor Maurice, outlining cavalry tactics and siege defense?
questions.explanation: The Strategikon is one of the earliest military treatises to describe stirrup-equipped cavalry and defensive combined arms.

questions.question: What catastrophic civic riot in 532 CE burned half of Constantinople and nearly toppled Justinian throne?
questions.explanation: The Nika Riots erupted over tax grievances and faction rivalry at the Hippodrome, resulting in an estimated 30,000 casualties.

questions.question: What precious ancient bronze horses originally atop the Hippodrome were looted during the Fourth Crusade and placed on St. Mark in Venice?
questions.explanation: The four gilded bronze horses of the Quadriga were installed on the facade of Saint Mark Basilica in Venice in 1254.

questions.question: Approximately how many casualties resulted when General Belisarius suppressed the Nika Riots in the Hippodrome in 532 CE?
questions.explanation: Imperial troops trapped the rioters inside the Hippodrome, killing roughly 30,000 participants and securing Justinian rule.

questions.question: Which fortified monastic republic on a Greek mountain peninsula has preserved Byzantine monastic culture continuously since the 10th century?
questions.explanation: Mount Athos (the Holy Mountain) contains 20 sovereign Eastern Orthodox monasteries preserving thousands of Byzantine manuscripts.

questions.question: What title was given to the co-emperor or crown heir apparent in the Byzantine imperial court hierarchy?
questions.explanation: Originally meaning supreme ruler in Rome, Caesar became a high court title below Augustus and Basileus.

questions.question: Which 9th-century Patriarch of Constantinople is remembered for sending missions to Christianize the Slavic nations and disputing papal primacy?
questions.explanation: Photios I was one of the most learned scholars of antiquity, author of the Bibliotheca (Myriobiblon) reviewing hundreds of classical texts.

questions.question: What legendary Christian relic was preserved in the Palace of Blachernae, believed to protect Constantinople from naval attacks?
options: Holy Mantle of the Virgin Mary
questions.explanation: The Virgin Maphorion (Holy Robe) was paraded along the sea walls during sieges, credited with stirring divine storms against invaders.

questions.question: What massive cannon cast by Hungarian engineer Urban was used by the Ottomans to bombard Constantinople walls in 1453?
questions.explanation: The Basilic was a super-sized bronze bombard over 8 meters long, capable of firing 600-kilogram stone cannonballs.

questions.question: In what year CE did Constantine the Great formally dedicate Constantinople as the new Roman capital?
questions.explanation: Nova Roma (Constantinople) was consecrated on May 11, 330 CE after six years of reconstruction on ancient Byzantium.

questions.question: Which Byzantine empress was the first woman in European history to rule as sole monarch in her own right, styling herself Basileus?
questions.explanation: Irene of Athens ruled from 797 to 802 CE as sole emperor, calling the Second Council of Nicaea to restore religious icons.

questions.question: What great library encyclopedia compiled in Constantinople in the 10th century preserved over 30,000 entries on ancient history and literature?
questions.explanation: The Suda is a massive 10th-century Byzantine encyclopedia preserving thousands of quotes from lost classical Greek authors.

questions.question: Which Venetian Doge led the diversion and assault of the Fourth Crusade against Constantinople despite being elderly and blind?
questions.explanation: Doge Enrico Dandolo orchestrated the Venetian fleet operations and was buried inside Hagia Sophia after his death in 1205.

questions.question: What Byzantine architectural technique used triangular curved masonry segments to set a circular dome over a square base room?
questions.explanation: Pendentives allowed Byzantine architects to float enormous spherical domes atop four massive supporting arches.

questions.question: What was the Greek title for emperor that became the standard formal designation for Byzantine sovereigns starting in 629 CE?
questions.explanation: Emperor Heraclius adopted the ancient Greek royal title Basileus to reflect the Hellenic cultural identity of the empire.

questions.question: How many total centuries did the Eastern Roman (Byzantine) Empire endure from 330 CE to 1453 CE?
questions.explanation: From Constantine foundation in 330 to Ottoman conquest in 1453, Byzantium survived for over 11 centuries.

questions.question: Which Italian city contains the world finest collection of surviving 6th-century Byzantine imperial mosaics at the Basilica of San Vitale?
questions.explanation: Ravenna served as the capital of the Byzantine Exarchate of Italy, featuring mosaic portraits of Justinian and Theodora.

questions.question: Which mountain citadel in the Peloponnese saw the coronation of Constantine XI Palaiologos in 1449?
questions.explanation: Constantine XI was crowned at the Cathedral of Saint Demetrios in Mistras before traveling to Constantinople.

questions.question: What ancient Greek architectural work inspired Byzantine domed cross-in-square (cruciform) church architecture?
questions.explanation: The cross-in-square layout of the Holy Apostles in Constantinople became the prototype for Orthodox churches worldwide.

questions.question: Which devastating pandemic struck the Byzantine Empire in 541 CE, killing an estimated 25 to 50 million people across the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation: The Plague of Justinian (caused by Yersinia pestis) devastated agriculture, military recruitment, and tax revenue.

questions.question: What precious natural purple dye extracted from sea snails was used exclusively for Byzantine imperial garments?
questions.explanation: Extracted from the murex sea snail along the Phoenician coast, Tyrian purple was worth its weight in solid gold.

questions.question: In what year CE did the devastating Plague of Justinian first break out in the Byzantine port of Pelusium and Constantinople?
questions.explanation: The pandemic broke out in 541 CE, recurring in waves across Europe and the Near East for nearly two centuries.
